title: Annotated component recipes — accessibility-first examples and migration matrix for tokens/buttons/tables/charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a new set of annotated, developer-facing component recipes for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts that prioritize accessibility, concrete do/don't guidance, and a machine-readable migration matrix. Deliverables: 1) compact recipe pages with annotated screenshots and ARIA/keyboard notes; 2) do/don't callouts for token usage and color contrast; 3) migration matrix (old token -> new token / CSS var / codemod example); 4) sample code (React and plain HTML) + CodeSandbox links; 5) a lightweight QA checklist and visual-regression references for the documentation site rollout.
acceptance_criteria: There are four recipe pages published on the docsite: Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts, each with at least two annotated examples (good / bad).
Each recipe includes explicit accessibility notes: ARIA roles, keyboard behavior, focus order, and contrast ratios where relevant.
Migration matrix CSV present in repo and linked from each recipe; a simple codemod example (rename map) included in the repo and documented.
Design review signed off by PM and Accessibility lead, and at least one engineering review comment addressed on the corresponding PR.
Docsite preview deployed to staging with visual-diff anchors (png/gif) for each example so QA can catch regressions.
Usage snippets include both React and plain HTML/ARIA examples and are runnable via CodeSandbox links.
Analytics event added to docsite for `recipe_view` and `codemod_download` to measure adoption after rollout.
tasks: Inventory current token names and usages across components (scan storybook + codebase).
Draft annotated examples for Buttons: primary/secondary/ghost, with states and focus styling notes.
Create compact table recipes: dense vs regular, row actions pattern, keyboard navigation examples.
Chart recipe: accessible descriptions, tooltip semantic pattern, color-blind palette guidance and contrast references.
Assemble migration matrix CSV and author codemod example (jscodeshift script snippet).
Prepare two visual-diff images per recipe (good vs bad) and upload to docsite assets.
Submit docsite PR and request engineering review; address runtime snippet rendering feedback.
Coordinate with Accessibility team for final pass and include approval note in PR description.
Publish to staging and run documentation QA checklist (links below).
migration_notes: Provide explicit token mapping: e.g. `--color-primary-500` -> `--rwd-token-blue-600` and recommended fallback for legacy CSS.
Document typical anti-patterns: using text tokens for borders, hard-coding token-derived values in stylesheets, and token-dependent math in component props.
Include codemod example: rename map JSON + jscodeshift command sample and short troubleshooting section (common false positives).
Add a migration checklist for consumers: audit usage, run codemod in a feature branch, verify visual snapshots, update tests referencing tokens.
notes: We intentionally keep examples compact (one viewport height) for quick scanning — long playgrounds live in separate sandboxes linked from the recipe.
Prefer direct screenshot annotations over long prose for do/don't guidance — designers reported higher effectiveness in previous study.
Charts guidance ties back to runtime advice from Platform: avoid gradient token blends as they can regress quantized renderers in some embedders.
Migration matrix will be a single source-of-truth CSV in `design-system/migrations/token-maps/` and referenced by release notes.
